founding_year.basis: Founded 1965 in Boston by Bill Elfers, Dan Gregory and Charlie Waite. The firm's own listings corroborate it from the other end: the earliest dated position in this base is Worthington Biochemical, funded 1967, and Charlie Waite's first attributed deal is 1968

history.source: the firm's own archived listings 1999-2026 plus contemporaneous press
history.basis: Written from the firm's own record: the 1999-2001 frameset pages carry the year funded, the outcome and the partner for the 1960s-1990s book, the 2005-2010 ColdFusion cards and the 2011-2014 Rails partials continue it, and the 2026 Sanity dataset carries the current portfolio. Exit values are from the acquirers' own announcements. Rewritten to the reader-facing shape (PRO-147, 2026-09-24). Not counted in the portfolio: the Israel practice, Greylock IL, which cut its ties in January 2015 and trades as 83North. The 1960s to 1990s record (Worthington Biochemical, Teradyne, Continental Cablevision, Stryker, ROLM, Cullinet, Ascend) and the exit values are in the basis above.
history.value: Greylock was founded in Boston in 1965 by Bill Elfers, Dan Gregory and Charlie Waite, and is one of the oldest venture firms still investing. Its record runs from Millipore and Red Hat to LinkedIn, Facebook, Airbnb, Workday, Palo Alto Networks and Figma. Now based in San Francisco, it raised a $1B fund in 2023 and its eighteenth fund in 2026.

investment_concept.basis: The firm's own statement, verbatim from its meta description, second sentence (the first is 'Greylock Partners is a leading venture capital firm based in Silicon Valley.'), read 2026-09-26; straight quotes are the only edit; also on the site: The map is blank again. (homepage headline) | We back category-defining teams. (homepage section headline). PRO-147: the thesis is the firm's own crisp statement; Erik chose the descriptive line over the homepage headline (2026-09-26). Published inside quotation marks, as the firm's own words (Erik, 2026-09-26).
investment_concept.value: “We are early partners of remarkable teams building companies that matter.”

investment_stage.basis: The landed distribution over 561 members: 79 Seed, 421 Series A, 60 Growth, 1 Pre-Seed. The Series A weight is real but partly a convention — §6 assigns Series A to a pre-2003 first institutional round, and 366 of the base's rows are pre-window
investment_stage.flag: the site publishes no stage filter, so the stage list is derived from the base rather than crosswalked from the firm's own vocabulary

investment_geo.basis: hq_country over the landed base: US 521, Israel 16, Canada 9, United Kingdom 6, India 2, and one each in Ireland, Brazil and China. Core is US alone; the §1 constant caps the core at two labels and no second geography comes close
investment_geo.flag: the Israeli rows are HOME-desk seeds of the current firm (Apiiro, Blockaid, Upwind, Kodem, Dazz), not the Greylock IL book, which left with 83North in 2015 and is excluded

investment_scope.basis: The firm's own seven portfolioCategory values crosswalked (Applications->SaaS, Consumer, Cybersecurity->Security, Deep Tech->Industrial & Robotics, Fintech, Infrastructure->Data Infrastructure) and reconciled against the landed focus distribution, which puts Data Infrastructure 92, SaaS 82, Consumer 71, Security 53, Industrial 50, AI 36 and Fintech 31 above the 25-row floor
investment_scope.flag: RECONCILIATION FLAG, §11: two sectors clear the floor in the base and appear nowhere in the firm's own vocabulary. Healthcare & Bio is 64 rows — Millipore, Stryker, Genetics Institute, Vertex, Millennium, Exact Sciences — and Media, Gaming & Advertising is 46. Both are almost entirely pre-2010: the firm's current site has no healthcare category at all. That is a positioning-versus-history gap rather than an error, and it is flagged rather than added

investment_range.basis: Median $17.0M is the Form D first-round distribution over the 57 members with issuer coverage (p25 $7.0M, p75 $40.0M, max $1.50B). The lower limit is the firm's own smallest documented first check, the $250K it put into Palo Alto Networks in 2005; the upper limit is what the fund ladder supports at a 10-15% single-position concentration of a $1B flagship
investment_range.flag: a round-size proxy for check size, fair only for a lead investor. Greylock leads or co-leads most first rounds, but the median is the ROUND, not the check. The distribution also skews high because Form D coverage starts in 2008 and misses the seed-scale entries of the 1990s book entirely

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first: the names a general reader would recognise first (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24). Each is tied to its portfolio row by `slugs`; names read as a reader knows them, without legal suffixes (COLLECTION.md §8). Previously listed (20): LinkedIn, Facebook, Airbnb, Workday, Palo Alto Networks, Figma, Coinbase, Discord, Dropbox, Docker, Cloudera, Nextdoor, Instagram, Roblox, Okta, Rubrik, Wiz, Anthropic, OpenAI, Red Hat.

aum.basis: Form ADV Section 7.B, annual amendment filed 2026-03-31: 13 private funds with $10,469,154,000 of gross assets. Greylock Management Corporation is an EXEMPT REPORTING ADVISER (CRD 161537, SEC file 802-74573) and files no Item 5.F regulatory AUM, so both ends of the range are the sworn 7.B composite
aum.flag: the firm CODES its funds in the ADV under rule 204-2(d), which Part 1A expressly permits: every 7.B entry is named '9.1', 'FUND 3.2' and so on and no fund identity appears anywhere in the filing. So 7.B anchors the money and contributes nothing to the fund table below. The figure is gross asset value, not committed capital

funds.source: EDGAR Form D filings by the vehicles' own CIKs, plus press for the funds that file Indefinite
funds.basis: Greylock files two ways. Funds XIII, XIV and 15 report a real amount sold and those sizes are asserted against the accession at build time ($891.3M, $963.0M, $995.2M). Funds 16, 17, 18 and the IAI-1 series vehicle file 'Indefinite' at $0 sold and amend at close or never — the Lightspeed filing style — so their sizes are the press figures and the filing is existence corroboration only. Each numbered flagship carries a parallel -A fund and a Principals vehicle; those are counted in this basis rather than listed, as are Greylock Discovery Fund LLC and the GP entities
funds.flag: Greylock 18's size is not yet public: its Form D was filed 2026-06 at $0 sold and no close has been announced. Sizes for XII and earlier are press-based with no filing to check them against — electronic Form D predates none of them

hq_location.basis: Principal office on the newest Form ADV: 140 New Montgomery Street Suite 2600, San Francisco, CA (GREYLOCK PARTNERS, CRD 161537, Annual Amendment filed 2026-03-31). The firm's site lists San Francisco, CA; Menlo Park, CA; the principal office is among them, so the site agrees. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.

individuals.basis: The live Sanity teamMember collection: 64 people, of whom 52 are current. The CMS publishes a GROUP but no titles — the Creandum case in §11 — so the position is the group label the firm itself uses (Partner, Partner Emeritus, Venture Partner, Advisory Partner, Executive in Residence, Platform, Operations) and no title is inferred from LinkedIn or memory. The twelve people the CMS flags as departed are excluded. Social links: 26 of 52 people carry a LinkedIn or X link (26 LinkedIn, 19 X): 45 read off the person's page on the firm's site. 26 without a link.
